TreeNode is a caller-supplied ordinary object with data fields val, left and right, without getters, proxies or concurrent mutation. Every child is a TreeNode or the None. Node values are plain integers in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. There are at most 4294967295 nodes. targetSum is a safe integer. Every root-to-node prefix sum, not merely complete root-to-leaf totals, must lie in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. String inputs, when present, are ordinary str values, not subclasses. Integer values are plain int, excluding bool; lists are ordinary lists, not subclasses. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Allocation and runtime resource limits still require qualification; this declared domain is not a capacity or completion guarantee.
return: Boolean indicating whether at least one root-to-leaf path has values summing exactly to targetSum. A leaf has neither child. A matching non-leaf prefix is not sufficient; the absent tree returns false even for targetSum = 0.
mutation_aliasing: No node, value or child link is written. Input identities and caller-held aliases remain intact; local queues/stacks borrow node references only. The Solution instance retains no state. The private stack holds node references paired with scalar prefix sums. It is popped from the end, not retained as an append-only queue. No path or node is returned.
numeric: All node values, targetSum and each computed root-to-node sum are exact safe integers by precondition. Bounding only the final leaf sums would be insufficient because cancellation can follow an unsafe prefix; such inputs are outside the declared paired domain. No bitwise arithmetic or numeric coercion is used.
complexity: O(n + 1) worst-case time and O(h + 1) auxiliary space for height h, with O(1) for an absent tree. A binary depth-first stack holds at most one pending sibling per ancestor plus the active frontier. Each node is pushed/popped at most once before early success; each stack record contains one node reference and one integer. There is no recursion.
